sentences.text:
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 3761 of 2022
Applicant :- Dharmendra Rajbhar

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Bhupendra Kumar Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Anurag Upadhyay,Manish Ojha,Ramesh Kumar Chaurasia,Sh
Hon'ble Mrs. Jyotsna Sharma,J.
1. Heard Sri Sandeep Dubey through video conferencing and Sri Rahul Pandey, Advocates holding
brief for Sri Bhupendra Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Manish Ojha,
learned counsel for the informant and Sri O.P. Mishra, learned A.G.A. for the State.
2.

The instant anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with a prayer to
release him on anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 0031 of 2022, under Sections 376, 506, 507
I.P.C., Police Station Umbhaav, District Ballia.

3.  The first information report of this incident was lodged in pursuance of an application moved under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C. by the informant (alleged victim herself) with the allegation that the applicant was exploiting the alleged victim mentally and physically; the applicant is working in Indian Air Force; the date of birth of the alleged victim is 12.03.1999; on 25.06.2015 at about 11:00 p.m., the applicant forcibly entered in the room of the victim and established physical relations with her; he kept on assuring her that he shall marry her; meanwhile her marriage was fixed and was solemnized on 18.10.2016 with another in district Deoria; after the marriage of the informant, the applicant sent various photographs to the husband of the informant which angered her husband and therefore was sent to her parental house; it was further alleged that again the applicant started pressuring her for physical relations with the informant and has been sending her money regularly in her account for her daily expenses.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the applicant submit that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case; the applicant and the alleged victim were having a consensual relationship; in fact the alleged victim had lured the applicant into her net with association of other persons and she had been blackmailing the applicant and has been extroting money from the applicant; the alleged victim had started extortion of money since 31.01.2020, which is evident from the bank statement of the alleged victim bearing A/c No.2836810037451; up till 01.03.2021 the applicant had transferred Rs.9 lacs to the alleged victim, copy of the bank statement has been annexed on page no. 5 onward of the supplementary affidavit and the alleged victim was continuously putting pressure on the applicant to give her money otherwise the alleged victim will lodge false first information report against the applicant; when the alleged victim had demanded more money, then the applicant lodged the first information report against 21 named persons including the alleged victim (present informant), which was registered as Case Crime No.0147 of 2021, under Sections 388, 389, 420, 506 I.P.C., Police Station Umbhaav, district Ballia against the informant and her associates and in the said matter the police has submitted the charge sheet against the alleged victim and others; in the said matter the alleged victim was arrested and released on conditional bail; aggrieved by it, the present false first information report has been lodged against the applicant by moving an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.; the applicant has been nominated in this matter just to injure the reputation of the applicant by having him so arrested;
applicant undertakes to cooperate during investigation and he will not tamper with the evidence in any way.

5. Learned counsel for the first informant and learned A.G.A. have opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail of the applicant.
6.

In case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694, it has been held by the Supreme Court that while deciding anticipatory bail, Court must consider nature and gravity of accusation, antecedent of accused, possibility of accused to flee from justice and that Court must evaluate entire available material against the accused carefully and that the exact role of the accused has also to be taken into consideration.

entities.text: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. In the instant case, I considered submissions of both the sides, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case including the contents of the FIR, the statement given by the victim, the bank statement furnished by the applicant from which it is prima facie shown that the applicant consistently transferred money to the victim from January 2020 to March 2021; it may be noted that in this case, an FIR has been lodged by the applicant in the month of October 2021 against a number of persons including the first informant alleging that all the persons have been, in a well planned manner targeting the persons to extort money by obtaining their obscene video preceded by luring them into establishing physical relations; admittedly in that case crime no. 0147 of 2021 under Sections 388, 389, 420 and 506 IPC, the chargesheet has also been submitted.

In view of the above, I find sufficient grounds for grant of anticipatory bail and confirm the order dated 26.05.2022.
8.

Let the applicant, Dharmendra Rajbhar involved in the aforesaid case crime number be released on anticipatory bail on furnishing a personal bond with two sureties each of the same amount to the Dharmendra Rajbhar vs State Of U.P And 3 Others on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40685638/
2 satisfaction of the court concerned, subject to the conditions as below:-

sentences.text: 9. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court below shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.
10. It is made clear that observations made herein shall not in any way influence the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion, based on material before him, at any stage of the case.
